issue_context.title: Somfy MyLink can't connect on startup most of the time
issue_context.body:
<!-- READ THIS FIRST:
  - If you need additional help with this template, please refer to https://www.home-assistant.io/help/reporting_issues/
  - Make sure you are running the latest version of Home Assistant before reporting an issue: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/releases
  - Do not report issues for integrations if you are using custom components or integrations.
  - Provide as many details as possible. Paste logs, configuration samples and code into the backticks.
  DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! Otherwise, your issue may be closed without comment.
-->
## The problem
<!-- 
  Describe the issue you are experiencing here to communicate to the
  maintainers. Tell us what you were trying to do and what happened.
-->

It seems that the Somfy MyLink is not always ready to be established (see error below) most of the time at reboot.
I almost gave up but then decided to upgrade to 2020.12 when all of a sudden, the connection was working fine. 
Then, after the next reboot, it seemed that the connection was lost again.
I tried if it will start to work again after an upgrade, so I upgraded to 2020.12.1 but I still get the message that the myLink could not be reached (although it's perfectly reachable via Telnet).

## Environment
<!--
  Provide details about the versions you are using, which helps us to reproduce
  and find the issue quicker. Version information is found in the
  Home Assistant frontend: Configuration -> Info.
-->

- Home Assistant Core release with the issue: 2020.12.1
- Last working Home Assistant Core release (if known): 2020.12 
- Operating environment (OS/Container/Supervised/Core): Core
- Integration causing this issue: Somfy MyLink
- Link to integration documentation on our website: https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/somfy_mylink/

## Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml`
<!--
  An example configuration that caused the problem for you. Fill this out even
  if it seems unimportant to you. Please be sure to remove personal information
  like passwords, private URLs and other credentials.
-->

```yaml
# Somfy Living Room Shades (DHCP Reservation)
somfy_mylink:
  host: "192.168.1.22"
  system_id: "somfy"
```

## Traceback/Error logs
<!--
  If you come across any trace or error logs, please provide them.
-->

```txt
Logger: somfy_mylink_synergy
Source: /Users/home/Documents/HomeAssistant/homeassistant/lib/python3.8/site-packages/somfy_mylink_synergy/__init__.py:88
First occurred: 9:43:58 PM (1 occurrences)
Last logged: 9:43:58 PM

Connection failed for 192.168.1.22 on 44100. Please ensure device is reachable.
```

## Additional information
The mylink IP address and ID are correct, as I'm getting a valid Telnet response on that IP and port with that ID.
```txt
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","result":[{"targetID":"CC10781F.1","name":"All Shades","type":0},{"targetID":"CC10781F.2","name":"Left Shade","type":0},{"targetID":"CC10781F.3","name":"Center Shade","type":0},{"targetID":"CC10781F.4","name":"Right Shade","type":0}],"id":1}
```
comments:
I had the problem until I added an access point closer to the my link with its own ssid just for my link .

I've added retry support in https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/44977

review_comments: We don't need to use dict.get the first time since we've already checked for the error key.

The per-entity config is stored in the config_entry options based on the "entity_id" (which is the name reported from the API), which presumably could change and break the option storage. Given that unique_id is based upon targetID would it be more stable to use targetID for that config_entry storage?
I think that makes sense to do after YAML support is dropped in the future.  Since we want to import the existing configuration, I think it makes sense to keep it as-is for now.
If the user changes entity_id, this list isn't updated, it seems.
Will fix this when I migrate to using the unique id for the options.
